updateCooling() sets coolingOn true when temperatureC >= 8.0 and false when <= 4.0, then writes RELAY_PIN accordingly. Called in setup and every 250ms in loop after sampling A1. Relay is driven by temperature with hysteresis.

alarmRequired = doorOpen && doorOpenMs > 10000. On transition to alarm, tone(BUZZER_PIN,2000) starts. While alarmOn, LED toggles every 500ms based on (alarmElapsed/500)&1. Both buzzer and LED blink implemented.

setup() configures button, LEDs, buzzer, both ultrasonic trig/echo pins, and TM1637 brightness; loop() polls both sensors and calls controllerTick() which writes LEDs, buzzer, and display each tick, so distance and occupancy are shown from startup.

Green LED io_2 = io_7 && (io_6 >= 5.0). This depends on the parking sensor, not the entrance sensor. When a car approaches the entrance (io_5 true) but parking is empty (io_7 false), io_2 is false, so the green LED does not light to guide the car.

Buzzer frequency is graded by parking distance (2000/1200/800/400 Hz) when io_7 is true, and red/green LEDs reflect parking state, so distance-based graded buzzer and LED indication on parking entry is implemented.
When io_7 && io_6 < 5.0, io_3 = 2000 and setBuzzerFrequency calls tone() continuously each tick; noTone is only called when freq<=0, so the alarm persists while the condition holds.
Button edge detection increments mode 0->1->2->0; io_8 selects entrance distance (mode 0), parking distance (mode 1), or occupancyCount (mode 2), and is written to TM1637 each tick.

setup() initializes Serial at 9600, TM1637 CLK/DIO as outputs, buzzer and LED as outputs driven LOW, sensor pins as INPUT_PULLUP with initial state read, then calls updateFullState, displayCount, printHelp, printStatus; loop() runs sensor/full/restock/beep/serial processing, entering the counting runtime state.

updateFullState counts occupied shelves into count and assigns occupiedCount when changed; updateSensors updates shelves[i].occupied from debounced readings, so the count reflects the three sensor states.
displayCount writes the digit pattern for occupiedCount to the TM1637; it is called on count change and in setup, so the current occupied layer count is shown.

checkRestock fires when a shelf is empty, not yet reported, and now-emptySince >= emptyTimeoutMs, printing 'restock needed: layer N'. emptySince is set on transition to empty and at setup, so the timeout is measured from emptiness.

When occupiedCount reaches 3, updateFullState sets recordsLocked=true, prints FULL lock message, and startFullBeep begins a 3-pulse beep pattern; while locked, new occupied transitions and ADD commands are rejected, so new records are locked.
STATUS or ? with no argument calls printStatus, which prints occupied count, lock state, timeout, and per-layer OCCUPIED/EMPTY, empty_ms, restock, and records.
RESET with no arg or ALL resets all shelves' emptySince to now and clears restockReported; RESET 1/2/3 resets the selected layer, restarting the empty timer.

setup() initializes Serial, A0, A1, D2, D5, D6, D13, and TM1637 with CLK=4/DIO=3; loop() samples all three inputs every 10ms and drives outputs, so real-time monitoring is entered. The requirement text says DIO=D5 but the resolved device and code use D3; the checklist expected value names D3, matching the code.

With vibration low, temp>=0 and <30, and current>=0, stateCode becomes 1 (normal). But the requirement's four states are normal/overload/overheat/mechanical; the code's normal branch requires io_0>=0 and otherwise sets stateCode=0, and there is no distinct overload state (stateCode 1 is used for current>=0, not overload). The normal output is produced when all inputs are in range, so the normal-state obligation is met.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
When temp io_1>=30, stateCode=3, and the fan output is set to 255 via analogWrite(5,...) because stateCode==3 maps to 255.0. So overheat turns on the fan at full PWM.
When vibration io_2 is high, stateCode=4 and faultCode=1; faultCode!=0 sets buzzer frequency 2000 and LED on, and serial prints fault_code. So mechanical fault triggers alarm and fault code output.

The vibration branch is checked first (lines 55-65) and sets stateCode=4/faultCode=1 before the temperature/current else branch, so when vibration and overheat/overload coincide, mechanical fault wins and faultCode=1 is output. The buzzer uses 2000 Hz and serial prints fault_code.

The TM1637 is only ever shown hw_value_io_6, which is stateCode (or 40 when faultCode!=0). Current io_0 and temperature io_1 are never written to the display; there is no rotation among current, temperature, and state number. So the required alternating display is not implemented.

When stock is 0, dispenseItem takes the else branch: prints error:outofstock:itemX, shows error code item*100 on display, and beeps three times (alarm). Error code and alarm are both present.
Holding D7 for >=1200ms in normal mode sets adminMode=true, displays 8888, and beeps. Long press entry is implemented.

In admin mode, readLineFromSerial feeds processAdminCommand, which handles add:itemX:N, stock:itemX:N, setprice, and price commands, updating stockArr/priceArr. Serial restock updates the corresponding item's stock.

setup() configures A0/A1 as INPUT, D2 INPUT_PULLUP, D5/D6/D13 outputs, TM1637 CLK D4 output and DIO D3, Serial.begin(9600), then calls sampleSensors/updateStateAndOutputs/updateDisplay and loop continuously samples. All required devices initialized and monitoring entered.

With currentRmsA<5, temperatureC<60, no vibration, overloadActive/overheatActive/mechanicalActive all false, nextState=NORMAL; printTelemetry prints STATE=NORMAL and FAULT=F00, LED HIGH. Normal state output produced.
When currentRmsA>=5.0 overloadActive latches true; with no mechanical/overheat, nextState=OVERLOAD, telemetry prints OVERLOAD and FAULT=F01. Overload state output implemented.

temperatureC>=60 sets overheatActive; nextState=OVERHEAT (unless mechanical), telemetry prints OVERHEAT, and fanPwm computed from temperature and analogWrite(FAN_PIN,fanPwm) with FAN_MIN_PWM..255, so fan turns on.

Vibration LOW debounced sets mechanicalActive; nextState=MECHANICAL_FAULT has highest priority; beep toggles tone on D6 at 2400Hz and printTelemetry outputs FAULT=F03. Priority alarm and fault code present.

The ternary chain checks mechanicalActive first, so when mechanical and overheat/overload coexist nextState=MECHANICAL_FAULT; buzzer uses 2400Hz mechanical pattern and telemetry FAULT=F03. Mechanical priority holds.

displayPage cycles 0,1,2 every 2000ms; page0 shows current (A prefix), page1 temperature (C prefix), page2 shows S and state digit. updateDisplay writes via TM1637 driver on D4/D3. Rotating display of current, temperature, state number implemented.
D2 button toggles manualMode in handleButtons; updateOutputs selects manual vs automatic values based on manualMode, so both modes are reachable and used.
In auto mode, temperatureC drives autoFanOn with hysteresis and computes automaticFanPWM from FAN_MIN_PWM to 255; fanPWM is written to FAN_PIN (D5) via analogWrite.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets modeIsSetting=false (current-value mode) and fanOn=false; loop() runs ProgramPage1 every ~10ms, so temperature control and periodic fan toggling are active from start. Default display mode is current value (modeIsSetting=false).
When tempLastValid < targetTemp and not alarm, sysml_value_0=true, written to D10 HIGH. With target 37 and temp below lower bound, heater turns on.
When tempLastValid >= targetTemp, the < comparison is false, sysml_value_0=false, D10 LOW. Also alarm forces heater off.
fanOn toggles each valid DHT sample (every 2s) when not alarm, and D5 is driven by fanOn. So fan runs periodically.

High count increments per valid sample when temp>=38; at 6000 samples (~2s each = 12000s, not 60s) alarmActive set, driving buzzer D6 (2000Hz), LED D13, and serial print. The 1-minute threshold is not met: 6000 samples at 2s = 12000s.
Low count increments per valid sample when temp<=36; threshold 6000 samples at 2s sampling = 12000s, not 1 minute. Alarm outputs exist but timing requirement violated.
st.modeIsAuto toggles on D2 rising edge (io_11 && !previousD2Pressed), and applyOutputs branches on st.modeIsAuto for auto vs manual paths, so both modes exist and are switchable at runtime.
In auto mode with valid DHT, io_6 is computed from lastTempValid (0 below 30C, linear 30-40C, 1023 at >=40C) and written via analogWrite to D5. Temperature comes from DHT11 on D7.
In auto mode with valid DHT, io_7 = (lastIo3 >= 600) where lastIo3 is A0 light ADC, and digitalWrite drives D9.
In auto mode with valid DHT, io_8 = (prevSoilHumValid <= 400) where prevSoilHumValid is A1 soil ADC, and digitalWrite drives D10.
D3 rising edge toggles manualTargetIsFan, switching the manual control target between fan and LED/pump.
In manual mode, A2 (io_5) sets fanPwmManual (clamped 0-1023) when target is fan, and thresholds 512/256 set LED/pump when target is not fan; these feed the manual output branches.
tmElapsedMs increments by 10 each tick; at >=2000 it advances tmItemIndex cycling 0->1->2->0, and applyOutputs selects temp/light/soil accordingly and calls showNumberDec.

When DHT invalid (io_2 false) or light/soil ADC negative, io_9=1000 and applyBuzzerTone calls tone on D6. Note: A0/A1 analogRead never returns negative, so only DHT-invalid path is reachable; that still satisfies 'any sensor abnormal' for the DHT case.
When serial_0_trigger (DHT invalid or negative ADC) is true, a FAULT line is printed to Serial.

setup sets displayTemperature=false and peopleCount=0, then modelTick sets io_8=peopleCount=0 and applyOutputs calls showNumberDec(io_8). In loop, with no button press displayTemperature stays false so io_8=peopleCount, and peopleCount is forced to 0 by the io_1/io_3 branches. TM1637 shows the count (0) by default.
modelTick never increments peopleCount. Every reachable branch assigns peopleCount to 0 (io_0<=0?0:0, or 0). Entry-before-exit ordering cannot increase the count; it stays 0.
Same as R002: no branch decrements or changes peopleCount from 0; exit-before-entry ordering produces no decrease (and count is already 0). The required decrement path is absent.
Button edge toggles displayTemperature, and modelTick then sets io_8=floor(io_4) when io_6 valid, else 0; applyOutputs shows io_8. So pressing D2 switches display from count to temperature.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
When peopleCount==0, io_7=0.0f and applyOutputs writes analogWrite(FAN_PWM_PIN, 0), turning the fan off. Since peopleCount is always 0, this is the reachable state.
Source assigns TM1637_DIO to D3, not D5, so the claimed D5 conflict is not present in the code; fan PWM D5 and TM1637 DIO D3 are distinct.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (stageIndex=0, paused=true, completed=false), configures pins 2/3/7 as INPUT, 13 as OUTPUT, 6 as OUTPUT, and constructs TM1637Display(4,5); the state machine starts in a settable, paused configuration with three stage remaining values at 0. All required devices are initialized and the system enters the configurable three-stage state.
On a rising edge of io_0 (D2), the code adds 1000 to the remaining ms of the current stage (stage1/2/3 based on stageIndex). This is a real increment of the current stage's countdown duration.
On a rising edge of io_1 (D3), stageIndex advances by 1, wrapping from 2 back to 0. This switches the active stage whose duration is being configured.
On a rising edge of io_2 (D7), if not completed, paused is set to !paused. When paused was true, this sets paused=false, starting the countdown.
Same toggle: when paused is false, the rising edge sets paused=true, pausing the countdown.

The model never decrements any remainingMs value (no subtraction of elapsed time anywhere), and io_4 (tone frequency) is always 0 in both branches of the completed check, so no buzzer beep occurs. Stage transitions only occur when remainingMs<=0, which never happens after increments. No per-stage beep count logic exists.

io_3 is set to sysml_state_completed, and digitalWrite(13,...) drives D13. However completed can only become true when stage3RemainingMs<=0, which is unreachable because remainingMs is never decremented. So the LED never turns on.

Serial output is gated on hw_value_serial_0_trigger = completed, which is unreachable (remainingMs never decremented). Also the printed text is 'process_complete_total_ms' not 'process complete', and elapsed values are never updated (always 0).

Valve output io_1 is set true only when io_0 (near) && io_3 (valid) && io_2>=20.0. There is no timer/latch to hold the valve open for a fixed duration; the valve follows the instantaneous near+level condition each loop and closes as soon as the user leaves. No fixed-duration hold is implemented.
When near (io_0) and valid (io_3) but level io_2<20.0, io_1 is false (valve off) and io_5=2000 (tone on D6) and io_6=true (LED D13 on). Alarm is triggered and valve prohibited.

io_4 (percent) is computed from level and shown via showNumberDec; io_5 is used as tone frequency, not usage count. The usage count (sysml_state_todayUsageCount) is only sent to serial, never displayed on TM1637. Display shows only one number (percent), not both percent and count.

Serial output is gated by serial_0_trigger = io_0 (near sensor), not by any serial query/command. There is no Serial.read/available parsing of a query; statistics are printed whenever the IR sensor is HIGH, not on a serial query.

Pressing D2/D3/D4 sets selectedItemIndex to 1/2/3 (lines 72-84), and computeOutputs with io_3 low sets out_io_6_tmValue = selectedItemIndex (lines 151-153), which displayNumber writes to TM1637. However only the item number is shown, never a price; the requirement asks for both number and price. The display path shows only the index, so the price display obligation is not met.

On a fresh D7 press with stock>0, controllerTick decrements stock (lines 108-117) and computeOutputs sets trigger true and value0=1001/1002/1003 (lines 185-192). serialReportIfTriggered prints "dispense:item"+itemX+" code="+value0, so the exact text "dispense:itemX" is not produced (extra " code=..." appended). Also beepSoundOn is set true then immediately reset false in the same tick (lines 97-104), so no audible beep occurs. Both the exact serial text and the beep are violated.

When stock is 0 and D7 pressed, value0 becomes 901/902/903 and serialReportIfTriggered still prints "dispense:itemX code=90X" rather than an alarm/error indication; the display shows 901/902/903 via displayNumber. The requirement is to alarm and show error code. The display does show the error code, but there is no alarm (beep is suppressed as in R002) and the serial output is a dispense message, not an alarm. The alarm obligation is unmet.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

ProgramPage1 unconditionally sets *io_3 (pump) to false (sysml_value_0=false) regardless of soil, rain, or water inputs; digitalWrite(10,...) therefore always writes LOW. The pump can never turn on in auto mode.
Pump output is hardcoded false in all cases, so it is indeed not turned on when conditions are unmet; the required 'not on' behavior holds (though trivially).
No logic reads water level io_2 to gate the pump or trigger the buzzer; io_5 (tone) is always 0 and io_3 always false. There is no alarm on insufficient water.
Button edge detection toggles sysml_state_manualMode on rising edge (io_6 true and previous false), and previous state is updated each call, implementing mode switching.

loop() only calls shouldTriggerWinner() when !locked; shouldTriggerWinner returns false immediately if locked, and on first stable press sets winner=idx and returns true, then loop sets locked=true. Subsequent presses are ignored because locked stays true until reset. First press is recorded and later ones ignored.

After winner, locked=true; loop's contestant branch is gated by if(!locked) and shouldTriggerWinner also returns false when locked. Only resetSystem (called from reset handler) sets locked=false, so inputs stay locked until reset.
On winner, loop prints pressTimeMs (millis timestamp captured at lock) then comma then winner via Serial. Both timestamp and contestant number are output.
handleResetButton2 is called each loop; on debounced reset press (resetStable true, not active) it calls resetSystem(false), which sets locked=false and winner=0, restoring the抢答 state.
When reset held >=3000ms, handleResetButton2 calls resetSystem(true), which zeroes totalBets[1..4]. The accumulated stats array is cleared on 3s long press.

Item button press (stable LOW) sets selectedItem=i and calls renderDisplay; renderDisplay for selectedItem>=0 shows DIGITS[selectedItem+1] on digit0 and price digits (with decimal point) on digits 1-3, so item number and price are displayed.

When inventory[selectedItem]==0, showError(1) sets errorVisible and renders E001 on display, and startSignal(3,500,180,120) beeps the buzzer. Alarm and error code shown.
Holding D7 stable LOW for >=1500ms sets confirmLongHandled and calls setAdminMode(!adminMode), entering admin mode.

Pressing D2/D3/D4 (io_0/io_1/io_2) when not in admin mode sets selectedItemIndex to 1/2/3. The display value io_6 is set to selectedItemIndex whenever io_3 (confirm) is not pressed, so the item number is shown. However the requirement asks to display both item number and price; the display only shows the item index (1/2/3), not a price. The price is only encoded in the serial value (1001/1002/1003) on confirm, not shown on the display. So the display shows only the number, not the price.

On short press of D7 (io_3 rising edge, not admin), stock is decremented (lines 156-170) and serial trigger fires with value 1001/1002/1003, printing "itemX" + value. Beep is set true on rising edge (line 137) and tone 1000Hz output. So dispense output, stock decrement, and beep all occur. The serial prints "itemX1001" rather than "dispense:itemX" but the requirement says output dispense:itemX; the code prints "itemX" prefix. Actually the requirement expects "dispense:itemX". The code prints "itemX" + number, not "dispense:itemX". This is a mismatch.

When stock insufficient and confirm short-pressed, display value becomes 901/902/903 (error code) and beep sounds (beepSoundOn true on rising edge). So alarm (beep) and error code display occur. This matches.

Long press D7: io_3 true sets adminMode true (line 119). There is no long-press detection; any press sets adminMode true immediately, and release sets it false. The requirement is long press enters admin mode. The code enters admin mode on any press (not specifically long press), and exits on release. This is a violation of the long-press condition.

In admin mode, serial input is not read at all. There is no Serial.read/parse for restock commands; the serial is only used for output. No code updates stock from serial. So restock via serial is not implemented.

On subsequent loop iterations the toggle interval flips alarmPhase, driving RED LOW and noTone, producing blinking and alarm. displayDangerLevel is called on level change to show the level. All three required outputs occur.

When no danger, updateWarning sets dangerActive false, writes GREEN_LED_PIN HIGH, and returns after turning off red/buzzer. setup also sets green HIGH initially. Green stays HIGH in the no-danger path.

On the danger-to-safe transition (dangerActive false, wasDanger true), lastDangerDurationMs is computed as now - dangerStartedAt and printed to Serial with the duration in ms. This is the most recent danger event duration.

When currentTempC >= targetLow, heaterOn is false and setHeater(false) drives D10 LOW, so at/above the range the heater is off.
updateVentilation sets shouldFanOn = (elapsed < VENT_ON_MS) and calls setFan(true) driving D5 HIGH at the start of each cycle; ventCycleStartMs initialized in setup, so fan runs periodically.

In MODE_VIEW_SETPOINT, updateDisplay alternates between targetHigh and targetLow and displays the setpoint value on TM1637.

When temp > targetHigh continuously for ABNORMAL_DURATION_MS, newAlarm becomes true, alarmActive set, Serial.println("incubation abnormal") emitted, and updateAlarmOutputs drives LED D13 and buzzer D6.

recordWinner calls display.showNumberDec(winner,false) with winner=index+1, so the recorded player number 1-4 is shown on the TM1637.
recordWinner invokes tone() on the buzzer pin with a 100ms duration, producing a short confirmation beep.
roundLocked is set true in recordWinner and loop returns early while locked; it is only cleared in resetRound, which runs on reset press. So other inputs are ignored until reset.
recordWinner prints a BUZZ line containing timestamp_ms (the debounced press changedAt) and player number over Serial.
On resetButton.pressed, resetRound sets roundLocked=false, winner=0, and shows ready; on release playerEligible is recomputed from button states, restoring the contestable state.
When reset held with raw and stable LOW for >=3000ms, clearStatistics zeroes totalRounds and playerWins, guarded by statisticsClearedThisHold so it runs once per hold.

Pressing D2/D3/D4 in normal mode sets selectedItem and hasSelection and calls showItemAndPriceUsingMutable, which writes itemDigit*1000+price to the TM1637, so both item number and price are displayed.
On D7 release with hasSelection, dispenseItem runs; with stock>0 it prints dispense:itemX, decrements stock, and beeps twice. All required actions occur.
When stock is 0, dispenseItem takes the else branch: prints error:outofstock:itemX, shows error code item*100 on the display, and beeps three times as alarm.
Holding D7 while conf is true and elapsed >= LONG_PRESS_MS sets adminMode=true, shows 8888, and beeps. The long-press path is reachable in normal mode.
In admin mode, readLineFromSerial feeds processAdminCommand2, which handles add:itemX:N and stock:itemX:N by updating stock[itemIdx-1]. Replenishment via serial updates the corresponding stock.
loop() reads D2 via buttonPressedWithDebounce and toggles currentMode between MODE_AUTO and MODE_MANUAL; both modes are dispatched at line 350-351, so auto and manual modes are supported.
In auto mode applyAutoControls writes fan PWM on D5 based on lastTempC from DHT11: >=30 sets 255, <=28 sets 0. Temperature drives D5 fan PWM.
applyAutoControls uses lastLightRaw from A0 to set D9 LED HIGH when <=400 and LOW when >=550, so light controls the LED.
applyAutoControls uses lastSoilRaw from A1 to drive D10 pump relay HIGH when <=400 and LOW when >=550.
In manual mode, D3 button cycles currentTarget through TARGET_FAN, TARGET_LED, TARGET_PUMP via modulo 3, switching the controlled object.
applyManualControls reads A2 via knobPWM and applies mapped value to the selected target (fan PWM, LED PWM, or pump threshold), so the potentiometer adjusts the selected output.
displayPage cycles every 1200ms through PAGE_TEMP, PAGE_LIGHT, PAGE_SOIL and showPage displays temperature, light, and soil values on TM1637.
When anyFault is true, loop toggles buzzerOn and calls setBuzzer(true) which invokes tone on D6, producing an alarm.
reportFaultIfAny prints [FAULT] with sensor details over Serial when anyFault is set, satisfying serial fault output.

ProgramPage1 never computes a stage from vibration/water; io_5 (display value) is only 4 when endAlarmActive else 1, and endAlarmActive is never set true anywhere. So display is always 1 regardless of inputs; no intake-stage (进水) number is derived from sensors.

No wash-stage detection exists; display value is fixed at 1 (or 4 if endAlarmActive, which is never set). Vibration input io_2 is passed but never used in ProgramPage1, so no wash-stage number is produced.

finishCycle calls showStage(FINISHED) which writes showNumberDec(4). FINISHED is latched and displayed until next cycle. Stage 4 shown at end.

finishCycle sets alarmActive=true and alarmStarted=now. updateAlarm toggles LED every 300ms and beeps via tone() for 350ms of each 1000ms period while alarmActive. loop() calls updateAlarm each iteration including the FINISHED early-return path, so buzzer and LED blink until acknowledged.

buttonPressed debounces and returns true on LOW (pressed). When acknowledged && alarmActive, stopAlarm() sets alarmActive=false, buzzerOn=false, noTone, and drives buzzer and LED LOW, stopping beep and blink.

In cycleActive, abnormalWater = waterPresent || filteredWater>=1020. When quietFor>=120000ms and abnormalWater and !faultReported, Serial.println(F("wash fault")) executes. Long no-vibration plus abnormal water prints wash fault.

setup() configures D2 INPUT, D5/D6/D13 OUTPUT, initializes TM1637 with CLK=4/DIO=3, calls Serial.begin(9600), and loop() reads A0/A1/D2 continuously. All required devices are initialized and monitoring begins.
When vibNow false, tempC<65, and |currentA|<10, rawState=STATE_NORMAL; enterState sets LED LOW, fan 0, buzzer LOW, and reportToSerial prints STATE=0. Normal state is output.
When |currentA|>=10 and no vibration/overheat, rawState=STATE_OVERLOAD; enterState sets LED HIGH, fan FAN_PWM_NORMAL, buzzer LOW, and serial reports STATE=1. Overload state is output.
When tempC>=65 and no vibration, rawState=STATE_OVERHEAT; enterState and loop both write FAN_PWM_COOLING (255) to D5, and serial reports STATE=2. Overheat state with fan cooling is implemented.

When vibNow true, rawState=STATE_MECH_FAULT (checked first). enterState sets faultActive, buzzer pulsing begins in loop toggling D6, and reportToSerial prints FAULT_CODE with the computed code. Priority alarm and fault code output are implemented.

The vibration check is the first branch in the state determination, so when vibNow is true alongside overheat/overload, rawState=STATE_MECH_FAULT wins. enterState for mech fault sets buzzer pulsing and fault code, overriding fan cooling (fan set to FAN_PWM_NORMAL). Mechanical fault priority is implemented.

updateDisplay rotates displayMode 0/1/2 every 700ms and showCurrentAndTempFallback shows current (mode 0), temperature (mode 1), and latchedState number (mode 2) on the TM1637. Rotation of current, temperature, and state number is implemented.
D2 button toggles currentMode between MODE_AUTO and MODE_MANUAL, and loop branches on currentMode to call applyAutoControls or applyManualControls, so both modes are supported.
applyAutoControls reads lastTempC from DHT and writes analogWrite(FAN_PWM_PIN,255) when >=30 and 0 when <=28; D5 is FAN_PWM_PIN. Temperature drives fan PWM in auto mode.
lastLightRaw from A0 drives LED_PIN (D9): dark (<=400) sets HIGH, bright (>=550) sets LOW, with hysteresis between.
lastSoilRaw from A1 drives PUMP_RELAY_PIN (D10): dry (<=400) sets HIGH, wet (>=550) sets LOW.
In manual mode, D3 button increments currentTarget modulo 3, cycling fan/led/pump.
applyManualControls reads A2 via knobPWM and applies to the selected target: fan PWM, LED PWM, or pump relay threshold.
displayPage cycles every 1200ms through PAGE_TEMP, PAGE_LIGHT, PAGE_SOIL and showPage displays the corresponding value on TM1637.
When anyFault is true, loop toggles buzzerOn and calls setBuzzer(true) which invokes tone(BUZZER_PIN,2000) on D6, producing an alarm.
reportFaultIfAny prints fault details to Serial when anyFault is set, called after sensor read; Serial.begin(9600) in setup.

setup() configures red D12, green D13, buzzer D6 as OUTPUT, calls veh.begin()/ped.begin() which set Trig D8/D10 OUTPUT and Echo D9/D11 INPUT, and tm.begin() sets CLK D4/DIO D5 OUTPUT. All required pins are initialized to usable states.

When simultaneous is true, inDanger becomes true; updateOutputs sets red LED HIGH (steady, not blinking), buzzer tone 2000Hz, and TM1637 shows io_7 (3/2/1). Red LED is written HIGH constantly with no toggle/flash logic, so the required blinking is not implemented.
When not inDanger, io_5 = !inDanger = true, so green LED is written HIGH continuously each control tick. No toggling occurs, so green stays on in safe state.
On danger exit, lastDangerDurationMs is set to dangerStartMs, which is only ever assigned 0 on entry and never incremented. Serial prints 0, not the actual duration. The duration is not measured.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (warningLevel=0), Serial.begin(9600), pinMode for A1, A0, D2, D6, D13, D12, initializes TM1637 on D4/D5 with brightness, and drives outputs from initial state values (all LOW, no tone). All required peripherals are initialized and the state starts at normal level 0.
warningLevel is reset to 0 each update, then set to 1 if temp>=60 or smoke>=550. If no alarm condition, level stays 1. So a single mild exceedance yields level 1 (关注).
The two source reviewers disagreed.

toneRunning is set true only when warningLevel==2, and tone command is 2000 Hz when toneRunning. The tone is a continuous 2000 Hz tone, not intermittent. There is no toggling/periodic on-off logic; tone() is called once and stays until level changes. Requirement says '持续间歇报警' (continuous intermittent alarm), which requires periodic on/off. The code produces a steady tone, not intermittent.

When warningLevel==2, serial_0_trigger is true and loop prints 'level' + value and 'key_value' + value. The string 'fire alert' is never printed anywhere. Requirement explicitly requires serial output 'fire alert' at alarm level.

Display value io_6 = warningLevel (0/1/2) only; it shows the level number but not a key value. The 'key value' (temperature) is computed into serial_0_value_1 but never routed to the display. Requirement says display shows level number AND key value. Only level number is shown.
modeIsAuto is toggled by D2 edge (lines 152-154) and initialized true; both auto and manual branches exist in output logic (lines 243-286, 289-341). Both modes are supported.

In auto mode with valid DHT (io_2), fan PWM is computed from lastTempValid: below 30 -> 0, 30-40 -> (t-30)*1023/10, >=40 -> 1023 (lines 248-260). Output written to D5 via analogWrite(5,...) at line 559. Temperature controls fan PWM.
In auto mode with valid DHT, LED value = (lastIo3 >= 600) (lines 294-300), where lastIo3 is A0 light reading (line 523, 145). Written to D9 via digitalWrite(9,...) at line 560. Light controls LED.

In auto mode with valid DHT, pump = (prevSoilHumValid <= 400) (lines 322-328), where prevSoilHumValid is A1 soil reading (line 527, 146). Written to D10 via digitalWrite(10,...) at line 561. Soil controls pump.

D3 edge toggles manualTargetIsFan (lines 159-161), switching between fan and LED/pump targets. In manual mode, fan target uses A2 for fan PWM; non-fan target uses A2 for LED (>=512) and pump (>=256). Selection button switches current control object.

A2 (io_5) is read (line 531) and in manual mode with fan target, fanPwmManual = clamped A2 (lines 164-182); with non-fan target, LED = (A2>=512) and pump = (A2>=256) (lines 187-208). A2 adjusts the selected object's output.

tmElapsedMs accumulates +10 each step; at >=2000 it advances tmItemIndex cycling 0->1->2->0 (lines 217-237). Display value selects temp (index 0), light (index 1), soil (index 2) (lines 361-390) and is shown on TM1637 (lines 568-571). Rotates through all three.
Fault condition (invalid DHT, or A0<0, or A1<0) sets io_9=1000 (lines 345-359). Tone command 1000 is in [31,65535], so tone(6,1000) is called (lines 562-566). Buzzer D6 alarms on sensor fault.

On fault, serial_0_trigger is set (lines 393-401, 431) and loop prints "dht_valid" plus value (line 573). However the printed content is the fault flag value (false), not a descriptive fault message; still it outputs fault info via serial. The trigger fires on fault and prints a fault indicator.

When unlocked, each button's rising edge sets locked=true and winnerId; subsequent buttons are gated by the !locked check, so only the first press is recorded. However, all four checks run in the same call, so if two buttons are pressed simultaneously in the same 5ms sample, the later check (io_3) overwrites winnerId. For sequential presses the first is retained. The requirement is about the first pressed button; simultaneous same-sample presses are an edge case. The gating does implement first-press-wins for distinct presses.
winnerId is passed out as io_7 and written to the TM1637 via showNumberDec when it changes. On a press winnerId becomes 1-4 and the display updates.
The buzzer output io_6 is always set to 0 (sysml_value_1=0), so hw_tone_command_io_6 is 0 and noTone is called; no tone is ever produced on a press. No short beep is implemented.
After a press locked=true; the button checks are inside if(!locked), so further presses are ignored until reset. This locks other inputs.

serial_0_trigger is set true on a press but then unconditionally overwritten to false at line 161 before being output, so the serial trigger is always false and nothing is printed. Timestamp is also always 0.
D9 press sets resetting and resetAccumulatedMs=0 each call while held, so resetAccumulatedMs never reaches 3000; resetRequest stays false and locked is never cleared. A short press does not unlock.

resetAccumulatedMs is reset to 0 every loop while D9 is held, so it can never accumulate to 3000ms; resetRequest never becomes true and no statistics clearing occurs. Also no accumulated statistics variable exists.

setup() configures both HC-SR04 trig/echo pins (D8/D9, D10/D11), red D12, green D13, buzzer D6 as outputs, and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=D4/DIO=D5, calling setBrightness and showNumberDec to initialize it. All specified pins match the requirement.

When dangerNow (both distances <=80cm) is true, setGreen(false) turns green off, red toggles via redLedOn timing (setRed true/false), buzzer toggles via buzzerOn timing (setBuzzer true/false), and tm1637.showNumberDec(dangerLevel,...) displays 1..3. All three required actions occur in the danger branch.
In the safe branch (dangerNow false), setGreen(true) is called every sample, setRed(false) and setBuzzer(false) also called, and display shows 0. Green stays HIGH continuously while safe.

On transition from danger to safe (lastDangerState true), lastDangerDurationMs = now - dangerStartMs is computed and printed via Serial.print/println. This outputs the most recent danger event duration over serial.

setup() configures D2/D3/D4 as INPUT, D13 and buzzer as OUTPUT, initializes Serial, sets TM1637 brightness and shows floor 1. However it never displays the load percentage (only floor number 1), and A0 is not configured (analogRead works without pinMode but no load shown). The requirement to show current floor AND load percentage at init is not met; display shows only floor.

When A0>=900, overload=true; driveBuzzerTone(1000) activates buzzer. Floor change is prevented: the movement completion block at line 131 requires !overload, and line 138 resets movementRemainingMs when overload. However targetFloor is still updated by button edges (lines 107-109) even during overload, but currentFloor never changes while overload, so floor change is blocked. Buzzer active and floor blocked — satisfied.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

updateDisplay() only shows floor number (1/2/3, or 10 when overload&&floor==1). It never shows load percentage. loadPercent is computed only for serial output, not displayed. The requirement to display load percentage along with floor is not implemented.

setup() configures Trig D8 and D10 as OUTPUT, Echo D9 and D11 as INPUT, red D12 and green D13 as OUTPUT, buzzer D6 as OUTPUT, and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4, DIO=5 with brightness set. All required pins are initialized to usable states.

When both approaches are within 5cm, inDanger becomes true; io_4=inDanger drives D12 HIGH (red on, not blinking), io_6=2000 drives tone(6,2000) buzzer, io_7=3/2/1 drives display. Red is steady HIGH, not blinking, so the flashing requirement is not met.
When not in danger, io_5 = !inDanger = true, and loop writes digitalWrite(13, HIGH), so green stays on.

On danger exit, lastDangerDurationMs is set to dangerStartMs, which is always 0 (set to 0 on entry, never updated with millis). Serial prints this value, so the reported duration is always 0, not the actual event duration.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin, pinModes for buttons/A0/buzzer/LED, sets brightness, and shows hw_value_io_6 (initialized 0) on the TM1637. However the display shows only the floor value (io_6 = currentFloor), not the load percentage, and the initial display shows 0 rather than floor 1. The init obligation to show current floor and load percentage is not met; display shows a single number 0.

When loadPercent >= 80, overload true; io_4=1000 triggers tone(6,1000) buzzer, and overload branch sets movementActive=false and remainingSteps=0, and the movement-start branch is gated by !overload. So buzzer activates and floor change is prevented.

Button edge sets requestedFloor; when not overload and not moving, movementActive=true with 20 steps; each loop decrements; at <=0 sets currentFloor=requestedFloor and movementActive=false. Then serial_0_trigger = (movementActive==false && remainingSteps==0 && !overload) which becomes true on the completion iteration, printing movement_complete_ms. Delay is simulated via 20 loop steps.

The TM1637 display receives only io_6 = currentFloor (a single integer). loadPercent is computed and sent only to serial (serial_1_value_0), never to the display. The display does not show load percentage alongside floor.

setup() initializes outputs, sets showSetpoints=false (default current-value mode), and loop() runs updateTemperatureControl, updateVentilation, and updateDisplay each iteration, establishing the control/ventilation/display state. However, the display DIO pin is defined as D3 (DISPLAY_DIO_PIN=3), while the authoritative wiring requires DIO=D5. This is a wiring mismatch, but the item concerns entering the run state and default current-value mode, which is implemented. The default mode is current-value (showSetpoints=false), and updateDisplay shows currentTemperatureC when sensorValid. The run state is entered.

When currentTemperatureC <= LOWER_LIMIT_C (37.0), setHeater(true) writes HEATER_ON_LEVEL=HIGH to D10. This is reachable via updateTemperatureControl when sensorValid and not stale. Temperature below lower limit triggers heater on.
When currentTemperatureC >= UPPER_LIMIT_C (38.0), setHeater(false) writes LOW to D10. Also invalid/stale sensor forces heater off. Temperature at or above upper limit turns heater off.

updateVentilation starts the fan when !fanOn and elapsed since lastVentStartedAt >= VENT_INTERVAL_MS (300000ms), setting lastVentStartedAt=now and setFan(true) which writes HIGH to D5. Periodic ventilation is implemented. Note D5 is also the display DIO per wiring, but the fan logic itself is present.
updateButton debounces and on stable LOW toggles showSetpoints, switching between setpoint view and current-value view. Reachable from loop via updateButton(millis()).
In updateDisplay, when !showSetpoints and sensorValid, displayTemperature(currentTemperatureC) is called, showing the current temperature on TM1637. Default mode is current-value.

When showSetpoints is true, updateDisplay cycles pages showing Lo label, lower limit, Hi label, upper limit via displayTemperature(LOWER_LIMIT_C) and displayTemperature(UPPER_LIMIT_C). Setpoint values are displayed.

When temperatureCondition==CONDITION_HIGH (currentTemperatureC > UPPER_LIMIT_C) and elapsed since conditionStartedAt >= 60000ms, setAlarm(true) is called, which sets LED D13 HIGH, tone on D6, and Serial.println("incubation abnormal"). Continuous 1-minute high condition triggers alarm and serial output.

When currentTemperatureC < LOWER_LIMIT_C, nextCondition=CONDITION_LOW; after 60000ms continuous, setAlarm(true) triggers LED D13, buzzer D6, and serial "incubation abnormal". Low condition path is implemented.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin, pinModes for buttons/A0/buzzer/LED, and initializes the TM1637 display. However the initial display write uses hw_value_io_6 which is 0 (never set from currentFloor/load before first loop), so it shows 0 rather than floor 1 and load percentage. The required initial display of current floor and load percent is not produced at startup.

When io_3>=900, overload=true, io_4=1000 so tone(6,1000) sounds buzzer. Floor change is blocked: movement only advances when !overload (line 146), and overload with currentFloor!=targetFloor resets movementRemainingMs to 0 (lines 155-160). So buzzer activates and floor change is prevented.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

The display value io_6 is set to currentFloor (1/2/3) or 10 when overloaded at floor 1; it never encodes the load percentage. Load percent is only computed for serial output (100.0 or 0.0), not shown on TM1637. So the display does not show load percentage with floor.

processCommand parses two times via parseTime and stores them into reservationStart/reservationEnd with reservationValid=true; serial input path is reachable through serviceSerial/finishSerialFrame. Both start and end are saved.

reminder is true when reservationValid and clockSeconds < reservationStart and reservationStart-clockSeconds <= 60, i.e. within the last 60 seconds before start. GREEN_PIN is then toggled by (now/500)%2, producing a 500ms on/off blink. This matches the 1-minute-before reminder blink.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

When reservationValid and clockSeconds >= reservationEnd and occupied, overtime is set, "overtime use" printed, and shouldBuzz toggles tone on BUZZER_PIN in 250ms pulses every 2s. Both buzzer and serial output occur.
releaseButton is debounced on D7 with INPUT_PULLUP; when stable LOW (pressed), releaseRoom() clears occupied and reservationValid. This is the manual release path.

setup() configures heater/LED/pump/buzzer as outputs, button as input, initializes PWM outputs to 0, silences buzzer, initializes TM1637 brightness and display, and loop() samples all three analog inputs plus button every 10ms and calls controllerTick which drives outputs. All required init and control loop present.
io_0 is LM35 ADC on A1. applyOutputs sets heater PWM to 255 when io_0<250 and not alarm, else 0. analogWrite(PIN_HEATER,...) drives D10. Temperature-based heater control implemented.
io_1 is light sensor ADC on A0. LED PWM set to 200 when io_1<300 and not alarm, else 0, written to D9. Light-based illumination control implemented.

io_2 is level sensor ADC on A2. When io_2<300 alarmState becomes true, and pump D5 is set HIGH (on) during alarm. When level is normal, pump is LOW (off). The pump is driven based on water level, satisfying the protection control requirement.

When io_2<300, alarmState=true; applyOutputs then forces heater=0, LED=0, and tone(1000) on buzzer D6. So on low water, heater and LED are shut off and buzzer alarms. Pump is turned on (aeration) which is reasonable protection. Requirement 'close related devices and alarm' satisfied for heater/LED plus buzzer.

Button D2 read as io_7; on rising edge displayMode increments, wraps at 3 to 0. applyOutputs selects floor(io_0)/floor(io_1)/floor(io_2) based on displayMode 0/1/2 and shows on TM1637. Cycles through temperature, light, level.

parseCommandLine handles START/END/SET lines, parses HH:MM via parseHHMM with range checks, and stores into startMinutes/endMinutes with hasStart/hasEnd flags; loop reads serial lines and calls parseCommandLine. Times are persisted in static globals.

handleGreenReminder toggles greenBlinkOn every 250ms and calls setGreen(greenBlinkOn) when withinStartMinus1Minute() and not occupied; loop calls it when timeValid and !occupied. Window is [start-1, start) computed with wrap. Green D12 blinks.

startOccupiedIfNeeded sets occupied, red on, prints "occupied", and writes HHMM to TM1637 (not the literal word occupied, but display is updated). Requirement says display occupied; code shows time digits instead of 'occupied' text. TM1637 is a 7-seg numeric display; showing HHMM is not 'occupied'. This contradicts the display-occupied obligation.
handleOvertime: when withinOvertime and occupied, prints "overtime use" once and toggles buzzer via setBuzzerTone with 200/800ms pattern. Buzzer D6 driven by tone(). Satisfies beep + output.

buttonPressed detects HIGH->LOW edge with 50ms debounce on INPUT_PULLUP D7; handleManualRelease sets occupied=false, red/green off, buzzer off, clears TM1637, prints released. loop calls handleManualRelease every iteration.

evidence.text: if (lastBtn == HIGH && raw == LOW) pressed = true;

items.reason: setup() configures Serial, sensor input, buzzer/LED outputs, button pullups, initializes display brightness/clear, samples load, updates alarm, and calls updateDisplay() which writes floor and load percent segments to TM1637. All required initializations and initial display occur at startup.

sampleLoad sets overloaded when calibratedLoad > ratedSpan (raw>682). updateAlarm tones buzzer when overloaded. requestFloor returns early if overloaded, so button presses cannot start a floor change; updateMovement also pauses during overload. Alarm activates and floor changes are blocked.

Button press (LOW after debounce) calls requestFloor which sets moving and remainingTravelMs = 2000*distance. updateMovement decrements remainingTravelMs by elapsed each loop; when elapsed >= remaining, sets currentFloor=targetFloor, moving=false, updates display, and prints "movement complete". Delay is simulated via millis-based travel time.

updateDisplay encodes currentFloor in segment 0 and loadPercent hundreds/tens/units in segments 1-3, then setSegments writes to TM1637. loadPercent is computed from A0 in sampleLoad. Display is refreshed every 100ms in loop and at startup.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, configures A1/A0/A2 inputs, D10/D9/D5/D6 outputs, D2 input, initializes TM1637 brightness, and loop() runs the control update each cycle. All required initialization and the control loop are present.
io_0 is read from A1 (LM35). In ProgramPage1, when not in alarm, io_0<250 sets conditional_2=255 else 0, written to D10 via analogWrite. Heater responds to temperature.
io_1 is read from A0 (photoresistor). When not in alarm, io_1<300 sets conditional_4=200 else 0, written to D9 via analogWrite. Lighting responds to light level.
io_2 is read from A2 (water level). When io_2<300 alarmState=true, and sysml_value_2 (io_5) becomes true, driving D5 HIGH via digitalWrite. Pump is controlled by water level.

When io_2<300, alarmState=true. Then conditional_1=0 (D10 off), conditional_3=0 (D9 off), conditional_5=true (D5 HIGH), conditional_6=1000 (tone 1000Hz on D6). Heater and light are turned off, pump is turned on, and buzzer alarms. The requirement says close related devices and alarm; heater and light are off, buzzer sounds.

Button D2 read into io_7. On rising edge (io_7 true and previousPressed false), displayMode increments; if ==3 resets to 0. Display value selects io_0 (temp), io_1 (light), or io_2 (water level) based on displayMode 0/1/2, shown on TM1637.

setup() configures D2/D3 as INPUT, TRIG output, ECHO input, buzzer/LED outputs, D7 pullup, initializes TM1637 brightness/clear, Serial.begin(9600), zeroes counters, clears fullAlarmed, and displays 0; loop then runs counting normally. All required peripherals are initialized and normal counting state entered.

handleProximityCount on PROX_RECY_PIN (D2) increments recyclableCount on rising edge when not gated by fullAlarmed and hold time elapsed. lastProxRecy initialized in setup, so a real rising edge on D2 increments the recyclable counter.

evidence.text: handleProximityCount(PROX_RECY_PIN, lastProxRecy, lastProxRecyTrigger, recyclableCount, nowMs, isGateFull);

items.reason: handleProximityCount on PROX_OTHER_PIN (D3) increments otherCount on rising edge when not gated and hold time elapsed. lastProxOther initialized in setup, so a real rising edge on D3 increments the other counter.

evidence.text: handleProximityCount(PROX_OTHER_PIN, lastProxOther, lastProxOtherTrigger, otherCount, nowMs, isGateFull);

items.reason: loop computes total = recyclableCount + otherCount and calls updateDisplay(total) every iteration, which writes the total to TM1637 via showNumberDecEx. This runs after any count change, so the display reflects the total.

evidence.text: display.showNumberDecEx(showVal, 0b01000000, false); // no leading zeros, colon off

items.reason: When ultrasonic height exceeds FULL_HEIGHT_CM, fullAlarmed is set true; handleProximityCount is gated by isGateFull so counts stop incrementing, and the alarm branch toggles LED/buzzer via setAlarmOutput. Counting is stopped and alarm output is driven.
On the transition to fullAlarmed (first time threshold exceeded), Serial.println("empty bin needed") is executed exactly once. This matches the required serial output at alarm trigger.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

setup() configures A1 as input with analogReference, D2/D3 as INPUT_PULLUP, buzzer D6 and LED D13 as outputs driven LOW, TM1637 CLK D4/DIO D5 as outputs, Serial.begin(9600) for GPS input, attaches vibration ISR, samples temperature, and enters loop() monitoring. All required devices initialized.

sampleTemperature computes temperatureC from A1; when it exceeds 8.0C and not already in excursion, increments temperatureEvents, calls updateAlarm (LED HIGH, tone on D6) before logging, then logEvent(TEMP_HIGH) which includes lat/lon. Alarm and log both occur on the rising threshold crossing.

pollDoor debounces D3; on transition to open it increments doorEvents, calls updateAlarm (which requests alarm when transportActive && doorOpen), then logs DOOR_OPEN_IN_TRANSIT with position. Alarm and log both fire on open during transport.
vibrationISR counts edges separated by >=150ms quiet period into pendingVibrations; collectVibrations adds to vibrationEvents and logs SEVERE_VIBRATION. Count is recorded.

updateDisplay cycles displayPage 0..3 every 2000ms; page 0 shows temperature, pages 1-3 show temperatureEvents, doorEvents, vibrationEvents counts. Current temperature and anomaly counts are shown in rotation.
logEvent prints lat/lon from GPS-parsed values when gpsValid, else UNKNOWN. GPS frames parsed via parseCoordinates set latitude/longitude. Position included in event logs.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, configures A1/A0/A2 as inputs, D10/D9/D5 as outputs with analogWrite, D2 input, D6 output with tone handling, and initializes TM1637 (setBrightness, showNumberDec). loop() samples sensors and calls ProgramPage1 then writes outputs, so initialization and control loop exist.

io_0 is analogRead(A1) (LM35). Heater output io_3 is 255 when alarm disabled and io_0<30, else 0; when alarm enabled io_3=0. analogWrite(10,...) drives D10. Temperature-based heater control is implemented.
io_1 is analogRead(A0) (photoresistor). Lighting io_4 is 255 when alarm disabled and io_1<500, else 0; analogWrite(9,...) drives D9. Light-based lighting control implemented.
io_2 is analogRead(A2) (water level). Aerator io_5 is 255 only when io_2>0 and io_2>=10, else 0; analogWrite(5,...) drives D5. Level-based aerator protection implemented.
When io_2<10, alarmEnabled=true, which forces heater io_3=0, lighting io_4=0, aerator io_5=0, and tone io_7=2000 (buzzer D6). So low water disables devices and alarms.

Button io_6 is digitalRead(2). On rising edge (pressed and not previously pressed), displayMode cycles 0->1->2->0. Display value io_8 selects io_0 (temp) for mode 0, io_1 (light) for mode 1, io_2 (level) for mode 2, and TM1637 shows it.

setup() initializes Serial, both debounced sensors (D2/D3), reset button D7, TRIG output, ECHO input, buzzer, LED, TM1637 brightness, refreshes display, and takes an initial measurement; loop then runs counting when haveMeasurement is true. All required peripherals are configured and normal counting state is entered.

In loop, when not latched and haveMeasurement, a debounced inactive-to-active transition on recyclableSensor (D2, active LOW) calls recordDeposit(true), which increments recyclableCount and totalCount.
A debounced active transition on otherSensor (D3) calls recordDeposit(false), incrementing otherCount and totalCount.
recordDeposit calls refreshDisplay, which shows totalCount (saturated at 9999) on the TM1637. Both deposit paths update totalCount and refresh the display.

When fullnessPercent exceeds FULL_THRESHOLD_PERCENT, latchFull sets fullLatched=true; loop's counting branch is gated by !fullLatched, so counting stops. setAlarmOutput(true) drives LED HIGH and tone on buzzer, and the loop toggles alarm periodically.
latchFull prints exactly "empty bin needed" to Serial when the full threshold is exceeded and the latch transitions.

A debounced press on D7 (active LOW) calls handleReset, which re-measures, requires a valid recent measurement below RESET_THRESHOLD_PERCENT, then clears counts, clears fullLatched, turns off alarm, re-syncs sensors, and refreshes display, restoring counting.

setup() calls Serial.begin, pinMode for D2/D3/D7 inputs, D8 output/D9 input, D6/D13 outputs, tm1637Init() allocating TM1637Display on D4/D5, and initializes outputs to zero state; loop() then runs controlTick every 10ms and ultrasonic every 60ms, entering normal counting.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
totalCount is computed as recyclableCount+otherCount and tm1637ShowTotal(totalCount) is called each controlTick, so the display shows the total of both categories.

When fillHeightCmLatched >= 20.0, fullBinAlarmed is set true; counting is gated by !fullBinAlarmed so counts stop, and buzzerUpdate tones D6 and ledUpdate drives D13 HIGH, providing alarm. Counting stops and alarm activates.

On pressNext while not COMPLETE, currentStage advances modulo STAGES and remainingSeconds is set to the new stage's configured duration and displayed, switching to the next stage for configuration.

toggleStartPause: when state is IDLE, remainingSeconds is reset to stageSeconds[currentStage], lastSecondTick=millis(), display refreshed, then state=RUNNING; loop then arms the stage timer. Countdown proceeds in the RUNNING branch.
toggleStartPause sets state=PAUSED when state==RUNNING; loop then calls disarmStageTimerAndAccumulate. The countdown branch requires state==RUNNING so decrementing stops.

When remainingSeconds reaches 0, startReminderForStage sets BUZ_BEEP; updateBuzzer beeps buzzerBeepCounts[stage] times (1,2,3) with on/off timing, then BUZ_DONE transitions: if last stage sets COMPLETE, else enterStage(next, true) auto-advances to next stage in RUNNING.
On completion of the last stage, updateBuzzer sets state=COMPLETE and digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH); loop returns early in COMPLETE without ever writing LED LOW, so D13 stays on.
On first entry to COMPLETE, prints "process complete" then for each stage prints "Stage N actual_ms=" followed by stageElapsedMs[i], which accumulates actual elapsed ms per stage via arm/disarm.

D2 press while stopped: io_0 HIGH with previousStartPausePressed false toggles paused from false to true. But seconds never increments anywhere (line 136 is self-assignment), and running is never set true. The timer does not start counting; no increment path exists.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
D3 press with previousResetPressed false sets running=false, paused=false, seconds=0, buzzer off, displayValue=0. This resets the timer to zero.

displayValue is set to seconds each loop and shown via showNumberDec, but seconds never increments (line 136 self-assignment), so elapsed seconds are never displayed as changing. The display shows a constant 0.

seconds never reaches 60 because it never increments, so the buzzer trigger at seconds>=60 is unreachable. Also buzzerRemainingMs is never decremented, so even if triggered it would not stop after 1 second.

On a debounced rising edge for any bed, the code sets called=true, records callTimeMs=now, assigns order=seqCounter++ (preserving call order), logs the call, and recomputes top index; alarmActive() then drives LED HIGH and buzzerPatternTick beeps. Order and wait time are recorded and alarm is triggered.

On confirm press, computeTopIndex finds smallest order among called beds; if valid, waitedMs=now-callTimeMs, the bed is cleared (called=false, order reset), and logConfirmEvent prints CONFIRM bed HANDLED_WAIT ms. This clears the highest-priority call and outputs a handling log.

When a top call exists, waitSec=(now-callTimeMs)/1000 and updateDisplay(BED_NUM[currentTopIndex], waitSec) encodes bedNo*1000+tens*100+ones*10 with seconds%100. The display shows the longest-waiting bed number and seconds (mod 100). The requirement does not specify a range, so mod-100 seconds is acceptable; the bed number and seconds are shown.
Task specifies TM1637 CLK=D4, but the sketch constructs the display with TM_CLK_PIN=8 (D8), conflicting with the required D4 wiring.

setup() configures LED D13 output, buzzer D6 output, all three buttons via beginButton (INPUT_PULLUP on D2/D3/D7), initializes TM1637 with brightness/clear, sets currentStage=0, remainingSeconds=stageSeconds[0], shows it, and sets state=IDLE so the user can configure three stages. All required init and idle-configurable state present.

pressAdd in IDLE/PAUSED adds ADD_STEP_SEC (10) to stageSeconds[currentStage], clamps at 359999, and updates remainingSeconds and display. In RUNNING it still increases planned duration. Increase of current stage time is implemented.
pressNext advances currentStage = (currentStage+1)%STAGES, reloads remainingSeconds from stageSeconds and shows it, pausing if running. This switches to next stage for configuration.
toggleStartPause: when state is IDLE, reloads remainingSeconds from stageSeconds, resets lastSecondTick, shows it, then sets state=RUNNING; loop then arms stage timer. Countdown starts.
When state==RUNNING, toggleStartPause sets state=PAUSED, and loop calls disarmStageTimerAndAccumulate. Countdown logic only runs when state==RUNNING, so countdown halts. Pause implemented.

On remainingSeconds==0, startReminderForStage sets BUZ_BEEP; updateBuzzer beeps buzzerBeepCounts[stage] times (1,2,3) then BUZ_DONE; after STAGE_BETWEEN_MS, if not last stage calls enterStage(next,true) which sets state=RUNNING and loads next stage. Different beep counts per stage and auto-advance implemented.
When last stage's reminder completes (buzzerTargetStage+1>=STAGES), state=COMPLETE and digitalWrite(LED_PIN,HIGH). LED stays HIGH since nothing turns it off afterward.

In COMPLETE branch, printed flag guards one-time Serial.println("process complete") and loop prints each stage's stageElapsedMs[i] as actual_ms. Elapsed accumulated via disarmStageTimerAndAccumulate at each stage end. Output present.

setup() configures D2/D3/D7 as INPUT, D13 and D6 as OUTPUT, initializes TM1637 (D4/D5) with brightness and showNumberDec(0), starts Serial, and leaves paused=true, completed=false, stageIndex=0, so the system enters the settable three-stage state. All required devices are initialized.
On a rising edge of D2 (io_0), the code adds 1000 to the current stage's remaining ms based on stageIndex. This increases the current stage's countdown duration.
On a rising edge of D3 (io_1), stageIndex advances 0->1->2->0, switching the stage being configured.
On a rising edge of D7 (io_2) while paused, paused toggles to false, starting the countdown.
On a rising edge of D7 while running (paused=false), paused toggles to true, pausing the countdown.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
When stage3RemainingMs <= 0, completed=true is set, and applyOutputs writes PIN_LED HIGH when completed, so LED D13 stays on after all stages complete.

Serial prints 'process complete' and stage elapsed values, but elapsed timers are never updated (comment states they are kept as-is), so reported per-stage actual times are always 0, not actual durations.

When currentTempC >= 30.0, abnormalCount increments and isAlarmLatched=true; io_3=isAlarmLatched drives LED HIGH, io_4=2000 drives tone on D6, and serial_0_trigger is true so outputEventLogIfTriggered prints an EVENT line including gpsLat_x1e6. The two source reviewers disagreed.
While alarmActive, every 250ms alarmPhaseOn toggles and setAlarmOutputs writes LED HIGH/LOW, producing blinking.

The two source reviewers disagreed.
When alarmActive, ledState toggles each loop iteration; output io_3 = ledState && alarmActive, written to D13. So D13 alternates HIGH/LOW while alarm active, i.e. blinks.
When alarmActive, beepState toggles; io_4 = 2000 if alarmActive && beepState else 0. tone(6,2000) when nonzero, noTone(6) when 0, so D6 alternates between tone and silence — intermittent beep.
serial_0_trigger = alarmActive; loop prints "alarm" followed by the boolean value whenever trigger is true, so during alarm the serial outputs alarm.

showHumidity initializes to false in ProgramPage1_Init, so the display branch uses io_0 (temperature) truncated to int; with no button press the display shows temperature. However the display is only updated when hw_value_io_4 changes, and initially hw_value_io_4=0 while hw_display_previous_io_4=INT32_MIN, so setup writes 0; after first valid DHT read the temperature value is written. Default display is temperature, satisfying the requirement.

On each rising edge of the button (io_5 true and prevPressed false), showHumidity toggles. prevPressed is updated to io_5 each cycle, so a held button toggles only once. Display branch selects humidity when showHumidity true and temperature otherwise. Toggle behavior implemented.

When io_2 (DHT valid) and io_0>30.0, pwmCountFan is set to a nonzero value (at least 1 for just above 30, up to 255). The output io_3 is pwmCountFan when io_2 && io_0>30.0, else 0. analogWrite(5,...) drives the fan. At exactly 30.0 the condition io_0>30.0 is false so fan off, matching 'higher than 30'. Fan turns on above 30.

For 30<T<40, pwm = floor((T-30)*25.5), which increases monotonically with temperature (e.g., 31->25, 35->127, 39->229), and at T>=40 pwm=255. So speed increases with rising temperature above 30. The floor correction subtracts 1 when the product is less than its truncation, which is a no-op for positive values (truncation equals floor), so pwm = (int)((T-30)*25.5). Monotonic increase holds.
The requirement text assigns TM1637 DIO to D5, but the code constructs the display with CLK=4 and DIO=3, and the fan PWM also uses pin 5; the DIO is not on D5 as the requirement states.

setup() configures button input, heater/pump/LED/buzzer outputs, initializes TM1637 brightness and shows 0, and loop() runs periodic sensor reads and controlOutputs() every 300ms. Initialization and control loop are present.

LM35 on A1 is read and converted to °C; controlOutputs sets heater HIGH when tempC<26 and LOW when tempC>=28, preserving state in between via digitalRead of the output pin. This implements temperature-based heater control on D10.
LDR on A0 is read; controlOutputs sets LED HIGH when lightADC<=600 and LOW when >=750, with hysteresis via digitalRead of D9. Lighting is controlled by ambient light on D9.

Water level on A2 is read; when waterADC<=350 inLowWater latches true and pump D5 is driven LOW; when waterADC>=450 it clears and pump is driven HIGH. Pump protection based on water level is implemented.
When inLowWater is true, heater D10, LED D9, and pump D5 are all written LOW and buzzerAlarm(true) toggles tone on D6 every 250ms. Low water closes devices and alarms.

Button D2 press (active LOW, debounced >30ms, rate-limited 300ms) increments mode modulo 3, cycling MODE_TEMP→MODE_LIGHT→MODE_WATER. displayValueForMode branches on mode to show temp, light/10, or water ADC. Display content switches among the three values.

D3 debounce: on transition to LOW (pressed) after 30ms, calls handleLightCommand(false) which sets LED LOW. LED off.

setup() sets pinMode for LED (D13) OUTPUT, beep (D6) OUTPUT, TRIG (D8) OUTPUT, ECHO (D9) INPUT; A0 is read via analogRead which needs no pinMode. All four devices configured for detection.

When alarmActive true, beepState toggles each tick; io_4_tone_hz = (alarmActive && beepState)?2000:0, so tone alternates on/off producing intermittent beep.

showHumidity initialized false; setup calls updateDisplay() which takes the else branch and renders temperature (degree+C segments) with '--' when NAN. No button press needed, so default display is temperature.
handleButton debounces and on stable LOW toggles showHumidity and calls updateDisplay, switching between temperature and humidity rendering. Each press flips the flag.
updateFan: temperature <= 30 writes PWM 0 (off); above 30 computes fraction>0 and writes FAN_MIN_PWM+... >= 85, turning fan on. Strictly above 30 opens fan.
fraction = (T-30)/(40-30) constrained 0..1; pwm = 85 + fraction*170, monotonically increasing with temperature from 85 at just above 30 to 255 at 40+. Higher temperature yields higher PWM.

Requirement text assigns TM1637 DIO to D5 (conflicting with fan PWM D5), while resolved_devices and the code use D3 for DIO; the conflict is in the requirement itself, so the correct wiring cannot be determined.

loop() samples A1 every 10ms into hw_value_io_0 and passes it to ProgramPage1, which updates sysml_state_maxTempDegC whenever io_0 exceeds it (line 78-80). The max is persisted in a global and never reset after init. However, the raw analogRead value (0-1023) is used directly as the temperature without any LM35 conversion to degrees C, so the stored 'temperature' is not a real temperature reading. The requirement is to read LM35 temperature; the value is raw ADC counts, not temperature. This is a concrete violation of real temperature reading.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

On button press (rising edge of pressed), showMaxActive=true and showMaxRemainingMs=3000. But the countdown is never decremented: sysml_state_showMaxRemainingMs is only clamped to >=0, never reduced by elapsed time. So showMaxActive stays true forever after first press; it never returns to current temperature after 3 seconds. Concrete violation: no time decrement, so 3-second timeout never occurs.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

isDark = ldrValue < 500 and objectNear = distanceCm <= 20.0; shouldAlarm = isDark && objectNear. When both true, alarmActive becomes true and outputs activate. The 20cm boundary is inclusive (<=), matching 'within 20cm'.

BAR_A_PINS are D4..D13, configured as OUTPUT and driven directly via digitalWrite in updateBargraphSegments. Direct GPIO control of bar graph.
Both LED1_PIN and LED2_PIN are configured as outputs and driven by updateParityLeds based on parity, so both LEDs are used to indicate parity.

setup() writes analogWrite 255 to all six RGB pins. With common-cathode wiring, 255 duty on the anode pin means the LED is off (no current). All six channels are set to 255 before loop() runs, so both LEDs are off at power-on/reset.
raw1 = analogRead(A3) yields 0..1023; hue1 = raw1*360/1023 gives 0 at raw1=0 and 360 at raw1=1023, mapping the full pot1 range to 0..360 degrees.
raw2 = analogRead(A4) yields 0..1023; hue2 = raw2*360/1023 gives 0..360 degrees for pot2, matching the required mapping.
hsvToRgb implements the standard HSV sector algorithm: chroma c=v*s, hh=h/60, x=c*(1-|hh mod 2 -1|), six sector branches, m=v-c, scaled to 0..255. Both hue1 and hue2 are passed through it.
s and v are declared as 1.0f and passed to hsvToRgb for both LEDs, giving maximum saturation and brightness.
Computed RGB targets are smoothed and written via writeCommonCathode, which converts brightness to PWM (255-b) and calls analogWrite on the corresponding rgb1/rgb2 pins.
loop() continuously reads both pots, recomputes hue/RGB, and writes PWM each iteration with only a 10 ms delay, so colors update continuously as pots move.
The exponential smoothing (alpha=0.12) on cur values plus rounding to PWM produces gradual transitions rather than abrupt jumps; the smoothing state persists across loop iterations.
setup() sets angle1/2/3 to 0 and calls servo1.write(0), servo2.write(0), servo3.write(0) after attach, so all servos start at 0°.
setup() sets RGB pins OUTPUT and analogWrite 0, and sets all bar pins OUTPUT LOW; applyFromServoAngles with all angles 0 yields r=g=b=0 and ledsToLight=0, so all remain off.
applyFromServoAngles maps angle1 to r and setRGB writes r to RGB_R_PIN (pin 2 = rgb1:R).
angle2 maps to g and setRGB writes g to RGB_G_PIN (pin 3 = rgb1:G).
angle3 maps to b and setRGB writes b to RGB_B_PIN (pin 4 = rgb1:B).
mapAngleToBrightness computes angle*255/180 clamped 0..180, giving 0 at 0° and 255 at 180°, linear in between.
loop checks now-lastStepMs>=2000, toggles one servo per index, then increments currentServoIndex modulo 3, cycling servo1->servo2->servo3.
For the selected servo, angle = (angle==0)?180:0, so a servo at 0 moves to 180.
The ternary sets angle to 0 when it is not 0 (i.e., 180), so a servo at 180 moves to 0.
updateBarGraphFromRGB computes avg=(r+g+b)/3.0f from the mapped channel values.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
setup() writes hw_value_io_0/1/2 which are static-initialized to 0, so analogWrite(2/3/4, 0) drives all channels LOW. With common cathode wiring, all off at power-on/reset.
analogRead(A3) yields 0..1023. For io_3 < 341, sysml_value_0=1, others 0, so pin2 (R) = 255, G/B = 0 → red. First third (0..340) maps to red.
For 341 <= io_3 < 682, sysml_value_1=1, others 0, so pin3 (G) = 255, R/B = 0 → green. Second third maps to green.
For io_3 >= 682, sysml_value_2=1, others 0, so pin4 (B) = 255, R/G = 0 → blue. Final third maps to blue.
loop() re-reads A3 every 5ms and calls ProgramPage1 then analogWrite on pins 2/3/4 each iteration, so color tracks the potentiometer continuously.

setup() writes LOW to all nine RGB pins before setting them OUTPUT (common-cathode, so LOW=off), and writes 0 to each servo before and after attach, so at reset all LEDs are off and all servos target 0°. The 1s settle delay keeps LEDs off during servo movement.

SEQUENCE rows 0-6 are Red(H,L,L), Green(L,H,L), Blue(L,L,H), Yellow(H,H,L), Cyan(L,H,H), Magenta(H,L,H), White(H,H,H); loop iterates step 0..STEP_COUNT-1 writing each row's rgb to all three LEDs, giving the required order.
After writing each step's outputs, loop calls delay(COLOR_DURATION_MS) where COLOR_DURATION_MS=2000UL, so each color is held 2000 ms.
Step 0 (Red) angles are {0,45,90}, written to servos[0..2] via servos[i].write(SEQUENCE[step].angles[i]).
Step 1 (Green) angles are {45,90,135}, written to the three servos.
Step 2 (Blue) angles are {90,135,180}, written to the three servos.
Step 3 (Yellow) angles are {135,180,0}, written to the three servos.
Step 4 (Cyan) angles are {180,0,45}, written to the three servos.
Step 5 (Magenta) angles are {0,45,90}, written to the three servos.
Step 6 (White) angles are {90,135,180}, written to the three servos.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

setup() writes all three channel pins LOW before setting them as outputs, then calls setColor(false,false,false) which writes LOW to each pin. With common-cathode wiring, all channels off means the LED is off at power-on/reset.
analogRead returns 0..1023. For position < 341 (first third, 0..340), setColor(true,false,false) drives RED_PIN HIGH and green/blue LOW, lighting red on the common-cathode LED.
For 341 <= position < 683 (second third), setColor(false,true,false) drives GREEN_PIN HIGH and red/blue LOW, lighting green.
For position >= 683 (final third, 683..1023), the else branch calls setColor(false,false,true), driving BLUE_PIN HIGH and red/green LOW, lighting blue.
loop() runs continuously, re-reads analogRead(POT_PIN) each iteration, and re-applies the color via setColor, so the LED tracks the current potentiometer position.
setup() attaches all three servos and writes 0 to each before applyOutputs() writes the same 0.0 angles, so all servos start at 0°.

setup() drives all bar graph pins LOW and analogWrites 0 to R/G/B; applyOutputs() with all angles 0.0 yields r=g=b=0, sum=0, so every segment comparison sum>=threshold is false and all segments stay LOW.
RGB_RED_PIN is D2 wired to rgb1:R, and analogWrite on it is driven by angleToPwm255(servo1Angle), so servo1 controls red.
RGB_GREEN_PIN is D3 wired to rgb1:G, and analogWrite on it is driven by angleToPwm255(servo2Angle), so servo2 controls green.
RGB_BLUE_PIN is D4 wired to rgb1:B, and analogWrite on it is driven by angleToPwm255(servo3Angle), so servo3 controls blue.
angleToPwm255 returns 0 only for exactly 0.0 and 255 for any other angle, so intermediate angles (e.g., 90°) map to 255 rather than the linear value ~128; the mapping is not linear.
phaseMs accumulates 10 per tick and at >=2000 toggles the servo selected by servoIndex, then increments servoIndex 0->1->2->0, giving a 2-second cycle in order servo1, servo2, servo3.
When servoIndex==0 and servo1Angle==0.0, the ternary sets servo1Angle to 180.0; same pattern for servo2/servo3 at their turns, so a servo at 0° moves to 180°.
When the selected servo's angle is 180.0, the ternary condition (==0.0) is false and assigns 0.0, so it moves to 0°.
The code computes sum = r+g+b and compares against thresholds 1..15; it never divides by 3, so the average (R+G+B)/3 is not computed.
Bar graph pins are D8..D13,D44,D45 wired to A1..A8, but the segment logic lights all 8 whenever any channel is nonzero (sum>=1) and none when all zero; it never maps average brightness to 0–8 LEDs.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets activePot=0, then attaches servo and writes hw_value_io_6 which is initialized to 0.0, so command=0 is written at startup, giving 0 degrees.
btn1 on pin 2 is read as io_0; on a rising edge (pressed, prevBtn1 false) activePot is set to 1, and the mapping branch for activePot==1 uses io_3 (A3=pot1).
When activePot==1, output = io_3*180/1023, mapping pot1's 0..1023 to 0..180 degrees.
btn2 on pin 3 is io_1; on rising edge activePot=2, and the activePot==2 branch uses io_4 (A4=pot2).
When activePot==2, output = io_4*180/1023, mapping pot2's 0..1023 to 0..180 degrees.
btn3 on pin 4 is io_2; on rising edge activePot=3, and the activePot==3 branch uses io_5 (A5=pot3).
When activePot==3, output = io_5*180/1023, mapping pot3's 0..1023 to 0..180 degrees.
activePot is a single variable; each button's rising edge overwrites it, and the mapping selects exactly one pot based on the current activePot value, so only the last-pressed button's pot is active.
setup() calls servo1.write(0) before attach and again after attach, so the servo is commanded to 0 degrees at power-on/reset.
Debounced press of button index 0 (pin 2, btn1) sets activePot=0, and loop reads POT_PINS[0]=A3 (pot1) and writes the mapped angle to servo1.
When activePot=0, analogRead(A3) yields 0..1023 and map(potValue,0,1023,0,180) produces 0..180, written to servo1.
Debounced press of button index 1 (pin 3, btn2) sets activePot=1, and loop reads POT_PINS[1]=A4 (pot2) and writes the mapped angle to servo1.
When activePot=1, analogRead(A4) yields 0..1023 and map to 0..180 is written to servo1.
Debounced press of button index 2 (pin 4, btn3) sets activePot=2, and loop reads POT_PINS[2]=A5 (pot3) and writes the mapped angle to servo1.
When activePot=2, analogRead(A5) yields 0..1023 and map to 0..180 is written to servo1.
activePot is a single index overwritten on each new debounced press, so only the last-pressed button's potentiometer is read and controls the servo.
setup() attaches servo1 and writes 0 degrees; controller.activePot=0 and io_6=0.0, so first loop tick with no buttons yields io_6=0.0 and writes 0. Servo starts at 0 degrees.
On btn1 press (io_0 true, prevBtn1 false), activePot=1; then output branch activePot==1 sets io_6=map_angle(io_3) where io_3 is pot1 ADC. So pot1 controls servo.
map_angle computes adc*180/1023, mapping 0->0 and 1023->180; io_3 is analogRead(PIN_POT1) (A3). Output written to servo.
On btn2 press (io_1 true, prevBtn2 false), activePot=2; output branch activePot==2 sets io_6=map_angle(io_4) where io_4 is pot2 ADC.
map_angle maps 0..1023 to 0..180; io_4 is analogRead(PIN_POT2) (A4). Output written to servo.
On btn3 press (io_2 true, prevBtn3 false), activePot=3; output branch activePot==3 sets io_6=map_angle(io_5) where io_5 is pot3 ADC.
map_angle maps 0..1023 to 0..180; io_5 is analogRead(PIN_POT3) (A5). Output written to servo.
activePot is a single variable; each button edge overwrites it in order 1,2,3, and output selects exactly one branch based on activePot, so only one pot is active and last pressed wins.
setup() sets RGB pins LOW (off), shifts segMap[9]=0b01101111 to the 595 (digit 9), and attaches servo on pin 5 with write(0). All three initial states match the requirement.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
Loop iterates value from 9 down to 0, calls set7segDigit(value) each step, and delays 2000 ms per step, giving a 9-to-0 countdown at 2s per number.
angle = (9 - value) * 20 yields 0 for 9, 20 for 8, ..., 180 for 0, and servo1.write(angle) is called each step. Matches the mapping.
After the for loop completes at 0, loop() returns and is re-invoked, restarting the sequence from 9.
