items.reason: Each loop iteration updates RGB, 7-seg, and servo back-to-back before the single delay(2000), so all three states change together per step. Synchronous update is implemented.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which resets activePotSel=0, then attaches servo and writes hw_value_io_6 which is initialized to 0.0, so command=0 is written at startup, giving 0 degrees.
On btn1 press (io_0 true, prevBtn1 false), activePotSel is set to 0, and the mapping branch for activePotSel==0 uses io_3 (pot1 on A3). So pot1 becomes active.
When activePotSel==0, angle = io_3*180/1023, mapping pot1 (0..1023) to 0..180 degrees, then written to servo.
On btn2 press (io_1 true, prevBtn2 false), activePotSel is set to 1, and the branch for activePotSel==1 uses io_4 (pot2 on A4).
When activePotSel==1, angle = io_4*180/1023, mapping pot2 to 0..180 degrees, then written to servo.
On btn3 press (io_2 true, prevBtn3 false), activePotSel is set to 2, and the else branch uses io_5 (pot3 on A5).
When activePotSel==2 (else branch), angle = io_5*180/1023, mapping pot3 to 0..180 degrees, then written to servo.
activePotSel is a single variable; each button press (edge-detected) overwrites it, so the last pressed button determines the active pot. Only one branch is used for mapping.
setup() attaches both servos and writes 0 to each, so on power-on/reset both servos are commanded to 0 degrees before loop runs.
On a stable HIGH->LOW edge of btn1, analogRead(A3) is mapped via map(0..1023 -> 0..180) and written to servo1, satisfying the pot1-to-servo1 mapping.
On a stable HIGH->LOW edge of btn2, analogRead(A4) is mapped 0..1023 to 0..180 and written to servo2, matching the requirement.
Servo writes occur only inside the btn1Pressed/btn2Pressed edge branches; otherwise no write is issued, so each servo holds its last commanded angle until its button is pressed again.
updateButton only accepts a new stable state after the reading has been unchanged for debounceDelayMs (50 ms), and edge detection uses the debounced stable state, so presses are debounced.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets servo1Angle and servo2Angle to 0.0, but the servo write in setup uses hw_value_io_4/hw_value_io_5 which are static-initialized to 0 and never set from the model state before attach/write. So both servos are written 0 degrees at power-on. The initial position is 0 degrees for both.

On btn1 press (io_0 true, previous false), after debounce counter reaches 0, stablePressed becomes true and the rising-edge condition triggers mapping of io_2 (pot1 on A3) to 0..180 with clamping at 0 and 1023, storing into servo1Angle, which is written to servo on pin 4. Mapping and output path are present.
Symmetric path for btn2: io_1 rising edge after debounce sets servo2Angle from io_3 (pot2 on A4) mapped 0..180 with clamping, and servo2 on pin 5 is written.

servo1Angle and servo2Angle are only updated inside the rising-edge branches; otherwise they persist and are re-emitted each loop, and the write is gated by command != previous so the servo holds position.
Debounce implemented: on new press a counter is set to 5 and decremented each 5ms step while held; stablePressed only set when counter reaches 0, and reset on release. This filters mechanical bounce.
setup() attaches both servos and writes 0 to each, and model angles are initialized to 0.0, so on power-on/reset both servos are commanded to 0 degrees.

On btn1 press, after debounce counter reaches 0, btn1StablePressed becomes true and the rising-edge condition (btn1StablePressed && !previousBtn1Pressed) maps io_2 (pot1 ADC 0..1023) to 0..180 with clamping at boundaries, storing servo1Angle; applyOutputs writes it to servo1.
Symmetric logic for btn2: after debounce, btn2StablePressed rising edge maps io_3 (pot2 ADC) to 0..180 with clamping, storing servo2Angle; applyOutputs writes it to servo2.

servo1Angle/servo2Angle are only updated inside the button rising-edge branches; otherwise they persist, and applyOutputs rewrites the same value each tick, so positions are held until the corresponding button is pressed again.

Each button uses a debounce counter initialized to 5 on press and decremented each 5ms tick while held; the stable-pressed flag only sets when the counter reaches 0, and resets to 0/false when released, providing debounce before triggering the servo update.
ProgramPage1_Init sets segmentCount=0; setup drives pins 3-12 LOW from hw_value_io_1_segment_* which are static false, so all bar graph LEDs are off at start/reset.

On a rising edge (io_0 true, previousPressed false) pendingPress is set; with debounceMsRemaining==0 the count increments by 1 (segmentCount+1) and outputs segment_i = count>=i+1, lighting one more LED.
When segmentCount==10 and a new valid press occurs, conditional sets count to 0, so all segment outputs become false and display resets to 0 lit LEDs.

Debounce is not 0.15s. On a press debounceMsRemaining is set to 150 but never decremented; the next loop iteration sees it >0 and clears it to 0 and cancels pendingPress, so the window is effectively one 5ms step, not 150ms.

ProgramPage1_Init sets litCount=0; setup writes all segment pins LOW from hw_value_* which are statically false, so all 10 LEDs (pins 3-12) are off at reset. Segment outputs are litCount>=N, all false at 0.

On a rising edge (io_0 true, previousPressed false) with debounceArmed true, litCount increments by 1 unless it is 10; outputs are litCount>=N so exactly one more LED lights. DebounceArmed is set true after 150ms, so subsequent presses work.
When litCount==10 and a valid press occurs, conditional sets litCount=0, and all segment outputs become false (litCount>=1..10 all false), turning all LEDs off.
The two source reviewers disagreed.
setup() sets ledState=true and digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH) on pin 3, which drives led1 anode (mega:3 -> led1:A, cathode to GND), so the LED is on at power-on/reset.

evidence.text: ledState = true;                 // LED should be ON after reset/power on
digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);   // red LED on (active-high assumed by wiring)

items.reason: Idle reading is HIGH (pullup), lastButtonReading initialized HIGH. On first press reading goes LOW, debounce timer set, after 30ms currentlyPressed=true and previouslyPressed=false, so ledState toggles true->false and pin 3 writes LOW, turning LED off.

After first press previouslyPressed=true. On release reading HIGH, previouslyPressed updated false after debounce. Second press: currentlyPressed true, previouslyPressed false, ledState false->true, pin 3 HIGH, LED on.
Third press toggles ledState true->false, digitalWrite LOW, LED off, continuing the alternating sequence.
Fourth press toggles ledState false->true, pin 3 HIGH, LED on.
Each detected press edge (currentlyPressed && !previouslyPressed) inverts ledState and writes it to the pin, so the alternating toggle continues indefinitely.
digitalWrite only occurs inside the press-edge branch; with no new press, ledState and the pin output are unchanged, so the LED holds its state.

setup() calls initializeOutputOff for all six RGB channels and all eight bar pins, which does digitalWrite(pin,LOW) before pinMode(OUTPUT), so every connected LED channel is driven LOW (off) at power-on. Pot pins are inputs. All components start off.

selectColor returns 0 for reading<=340; setRgbColor drives all channels LOW then pins[0]=HIGH, which is RGB1 red (pin 2). For pot1 in 0–340, color1=0, and since previousColor1 starts -1 the branch runs on first loop, lighting red.
For pot1 in 341–681, first condition fails, second (<=681) returns 1; setRgbColor drives pins[1]=HIGH (pin 3, green) with others LOW. Correct green output.
For pot1 in 682–1023, both conditions fail and selectColor returns 2; setRgbColor drives pins[2]=HIGH (pin 4, blue). Correct blue output.
color2=selectColor(pot2) uses same thresholds; for pot2 0–340 returns 0 and setRgbColor(RGB2_PINS,0) drives pin 5 HIGH (red) with 6,7 LOW. Correct.
For pot2 341–681, selectColor returns 1; setRgbColor(RGB2_PINS,1) drives pin 6 HIGH (green), others LOW. Correct.
For pot2 682–1023, selectColor returns 2; setRgbColor(RGB2_PINS,2) drives pin 7 HIGH (blue), others LOW. Correct.

litSegments = (pot1+pot2)*8/2046 = floor(avg*8/1023). Average 512 gives 1024*8/2046=4 (4096/2046=2? recompute: 1024*8=8192, /2046=4.00 -> 4). setBarGraph lights first count pins HIGH. Proportional mapping correct; average 512 -> 4 LEDs.

With stationary pots, litSegments stays constant, so the if(litSegments != previousBarCount) branch does not rewrite; outputs remain latched indefinitely, satisfying at least 2 seconds. No delay or clearing occurs.

loop has no delay; each iteration reads both pots and immediately updates RGB (on color change) and bar graph (on count change). Adjustments are reflected in the next loop iteration, i.e., immediately.
setup() drives every LED pin LOW before setting OUTPUT, then progress=0 and updateDisplay() writes LOW to all pins since i<0 is false for all i. All bar graph LEDs are off at start/reset.
On a debounced LOW (pressed) edge, progress=(progress+1)%11. For progress 0..9 this yields 1..10, and updateDisplay lights i<progress LEDs, so lit count increases by exactly 1.
When progress=10, next press computes (10+1)%11=0, and updateDisplay turns all LEDs off, resetting to 0 lit LEDs.

DEBOUNCE_MS=150 and the accept condition requires now-lastChangeTime>=150 after the last reading change, so bounces within 150 ms reset the timer and are ignored; only a stable 150 ms transition is accepted.

ProgramPage1_Init sets activeAngleDeg=0.0 and activeLedLevel=0; setup attaches servo and writes command 0 (hw_value_io_4=0, previous=-1 so write(0) occurs), and all segment pins are written LOW since hw_value_io_3_segment_* are false. Servo at 0 degrees, bargraph off.

On btn1 press (io_0 true, prev false), activeAngleDeg=30.0, activeLedLevel=3, holdElapsedMs=0. Segments 0-2 true (level>=1,2,3), segments 3-9 false. Servo writes 30. First 3 LEDs lit, servo 30 degrees.
On btn2 press, activeAngleDeg=60.0, activeLedLevel=6. Segments 0-5 true (level>=1..6), segments 6-9 false. Servo writes 60. First 6 LEDs lit.
On btn3 press, activeAngleDeg=90.0, activeLedLevel=10. All ten segments true (level>=1..10). Servo writes 90. All 10 LEDs lit.

holdElapsedMs is reset to 0 on each button press but never incremented anywhere; the only code touching it is a no-op self-assignment. There is no timing gate preventing a new button press from immediately changing state, so states are not held for 2 seconds.

setup() sets activeAngleDeg=0.0 and activeLedLevel=0, then applyOutputs() writes servo1.write(0) and all segment pins LOW (since level 0 fails every >=1..>=10 test), so servo is at 0 degrees and bargraph is off at power-on/reset.

On a rising edge of btn1 (io_0 true, prev false), activeAngleDeg=30.0 and activeLedLevel=3; applyOutputs writes servo 30 and SEG0..SEG2 HIGH (3>=1,2,3) while SEG3..SEG9 LOW (3>=4..10 false), lighting exactly the first 3 LEDs.

On a rising edge of btn2, activeAngleDeg=60.0 and activeLedLevel=6; applyOutputs writes servo 60 and SEG0..SEG5 HIGH (6>=1..6) while SEG6..SEG9 LOW (6>=7..10 false), lighting exactly the first 6 LEDs.
On a rising edge of btn3, activeAngleDeg=90.0 and activeLedLevel=10; applyOutputs writes servo 90 and all ten segment pins HIGH since 10>=1..10, lighting all 10 LEDs.

The state is not held for 2 seconds: holdElapsedMs is only accumulated and never gates anything, and the button edge checks run every loop, so a new press immediately overwrites activeAngleDeg/activeLedLevel and applyOutputs() writes the new state on the same iteration. There is no condition preventing a state change before 2000ms.

setup() drives all 10 LED pins LOW before setting them OUTPUT, then calls servo1.write(0) and attach, then displayState(0,0) which writes angle 0 and all LEDs LOW. So on reset servo is at 0 and bargraph off.

Pressing btn1 (pin 2) debounces to LOW, enqueues index 0; after 2s hold, displayState(servoAngles[0]=30, litLedCounts[0]=3) writes servo 30 and lights LEDs 0..2 (pins 5,6,7) HIGH, others LOW. Matches 30 degrees and first 3 LEDs.
btn2 (pin 3) enqueues index 1; displayState(60,6) writes servo 60 and lights LEDs 0..5 (pins 5-10) HIGH, remaining LOW. Matches 60 degrees and first 6 LEDs.
btn3 (pin 4) enqueues index 2; displayState(90,10) writes servo 90 and lights all 10 LEDs (i<10 always true). Matches 90 degrees and all 10 LEDs.
displayState sets stateStartedMs=millis(); loop only dequeues and changes state when now-stateStartedMs>=MIN_STATE_MS (2000). Startup state also held 2s. Each state persists at least 2 seconds.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

loop() reads pot1 on A3, converts via adcToReal01_1023 (identity), then computeIo0FromPot1 and computeIo1FromPot1 both map 0..1023 to 0..255 using *255/1023 and clamp. These are written to RGB_R_PWM (D2) and RGB_G_PWM (D3) via analogWrite. The mapping and application match the requirement.
loop() reads pot2 on A4, converts via adcToReal01_1023, then computeIo2FromPot2 maps 0..1023 to 0..255 using *255/1023 and clamp, written to RGB_B_PWM (D4) via analogWrite. Matches requirement.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

loop() runs every 10ms (guarded by millis), reads both pots, computes outputs, and writes PWM and shift register each iteration. This provides continuous updates based on current potentiometer values.
loop() reads pot1 on A3 into rawR, maps it to r255, and writes that same value to both rgb1:R (pin 2) and rgb2:R (pin 5) via analogWrite, so pot1 controls red of both LEDs.
pot2 on A4 is read into rawG, mapped to g255, and written to rgb1:G (pin 3) and rgb2:G (pin 6), so pot2 controls green of both LEDs.
pot3 on A5 is read into rawB, mapped to b255, and written to rgb1:B (pin 4) and rgb2:B (pin 7), so pot3 controls blue of both LEDs.
map0_1023_to_0_255 clamps to 0..1023 then computes v*255/1023, giving 0 at 0 and 255 at 1023, a linear 0-1023 to 0-255 mapping applied to all three readings.

Requirement conflicts: task says sevseg1 shows red and green as two-digit numbers, detail rules say red mapped 0-255 to 0-9. Code implements the latter (single digit red only), so cannot be judged against a single unambiguous expectation.

Requirement conflicts: task says sevseg2 shows blue as two-digit number, detail rules say blue mapped 0-255 to 0-9. Code implements the latter (single digit blue), so cannot be judged against a single unambiguous expectation.
loop() unconditionally re-reads pots, recomputes digits, shifts out segment patterns, and rewrites RGB PWM each iteration with only a 5ms delay, so displays and LEDs update continuously.
The two source reviewers disagreed.

setup() drives all LED pins LOW before setting them OUTPUT, and applyState(0) sets illuminatedSegments=0 so every LED_PINS[i] is written LOW. All ten bar graph segments remain off at initialization completion.
applyState(0) sets servo1 to 0 and servo2 to 180, called at end of setup.
State 0 is applied in setup via applyState(0), which sets illuminatedSegments=0 and writes LOW to all ten LED pins, so all LEDs are off in state 0.
stateEnteredAt is set at end of setup, and loop only advances state when now - stateEnteredAt >= 2000, so state 0 is held at least 2 seconds after initialization.
applyState(1) writes servo1=90 and servo2=90, and the state-1 branch is reached on the first debounced press after lockout.
applyState(1) sets illuminatedSegments=5, and the loop writes HIGH for i<5 (pins 5,6,7,8,9) and LOW for the rest, lighting the first 5 segments.
After entering state 1, stateEnteredAt is reset to millis(), and the next transition requires now - stateEnteredAt >= 2000, holding state 1 for 2 seconds.
applyState(2) writes servo1=180 and servo2=0, reached on the second debounced press.
applyState(2) sets illuminatedSegments=10, and the loop writes HIGH for all i<10, lighting all ten segments.
stateEnteredAt is reset after entering state 2, and the next transition requires 2000 ms elapsed, holding state 2 for 2 seconds.
currentState = (currentState + 1) % 3 wraps from 2 to 0, and applyState(0) restores servo1=0, servo2=180, and all LEDs off, repeating the cycle.
The loop tracks raw button changes, requires 150 ms of stability before accepting a new level, and only advances state on a stable LOW edge, implementing 0.15 s debounce.
The state-advance branch is gated by now - stateEnteredAt >= STATE_LOCK_MS (2000 ms), and stateEnteredAt is refreshed on each transition, locking transitions for 2 seconds after each press.
On a valid transition, applyState(currentState) is called immediately in the same loop iteration, writing servo positions and LED pins before any delay, so outputs update immediately.
